rulings.decision: Allow landing-window exception for protected trailing-turnless-after-newest-closed zones
rulings.rationale: Approved: AC-5.3's protections are authoritative over the landing window when they conflict. The spec itself already contains this precedent — TC-5.2 requires the newest closed turn to remain intact even when it alone exceeds target, which necessarily lands the zone above target + one turn. Trailing turnless singleton groups positioned after the newest closed turn cannot be evicted without first evicting the protected newest turn, because the boundary is a positional marker advanced oldest-first; their protection is structural, not a new rule. Therefore the landing guarantee [target, target + one turn) applies only when achievable without violating the explicit protections. Keep current implementation and tests; update AC-5.3/tech-design wording to state the exception explicitly; rerun verification. This ruling will be surfaced at epic review for ratification.

Approved: (1) seedTurnedToolResults implemented as (sdk, filePath, turns) seeding through a real intake commit rather than the test plan's sketched (db, turns) signature — a direct-DB seeder could never fire the production advance since no host-called advance surface exists; the fixture drives the production path, which is exactly what the anti-shim rule requires. (2) The landing-window exception for protected trailing-turnless-after-newest-closed zones was ruled in ruling-020 (impl-lead approved, to be ratified at epic review) and verification has since passed (008-verify).
